takeaway: Hunter's (adductor) canal: lateral border vastus medialis; medial border adductor longus above and adductor magnus below; roof sartorius, fascia and the subsartorial plexus.

lines.text: Hunter's canal, also called the adductor canal, is an aponeurotic tunnel in the middle third of the thigh.
It runs from the apex of the femoral triangle to the adductor hiatus, an opening in adductor magnus.
Its lateral border is formed by vastus medialis.
That is this large muscle on the outer side of the canal.
The medial border is adductor longus above, and adductor magnus below.
The roof is sartorius, with fascia and the subsartorial plexus.
So the lateral border of Hunter's canal is vastus medialis.
